title: What Is an Earthquake
keyIdea: An earthquake is the ground shaking when pieces of Earth's crust (plates) bump, scrape, or slide. Stay safe with Drop, Cover, Hold.
familyTip: Shake a jelly on a plate to show ground motion. Practise Drop-Cover-Hold under a sturdy table. Contrast with volcano ash/lava pictures.

visual.caption: Earthquake idea or mix-up? Drag each clue, or tap it and then tap a box.

items: plates bumping can shake the ground
Drop, Cover, Hold is a safety plan
sudden ground shake is a quake clue
earth always opens a forever canyon
Earth's shell is cracked into plates

lab.caption: Flagship lab: crack the crust into plates, shake the ground, name the cause, sort quake clues, practise Drop-Cover-Hold, reject canyon myths, then challenge.

kid: Earth's outer shell is cracked into big pieces called plates.
When plates bump or slide, the ground can shake.
If it shakes, Drop low, Cover your head, and Hold on.
adult: KS1 rocks/earth & hazards: earthquakes as ground shaking from plate motion (simple plate idea). Words: plate, crust, shake, Drop Cover Hold. Distinct from volcanoes (magma/ash).
Common mistakes: thinking quakes are only thunder or rain; cartoon forever canyons; running to windows; mixing volcano ash with quake shake.
In the lab your child adds plate cracks, shakes the ground, picks the true cause, sorts clues, practises Drop-Cover-Hold, and rejects canyon myths.

practice.hint: Think about what the ground does in an earthquake.
practice.explain: An earthquake means the ground shakes when plates move.

practice.hint: Look under the ground for moving plates, not the sky.
practice.explain: Moving plates bump or slide and can shake the ground.

practice.prompt: Drop-Cover-Hold steps stay 3 even if you practise {n} times — type 3.
practice.hint: The plan always has three named moves no matter the practice count.
practice.explain: Practising {n} times still leaves 3 steps: Drop, Cover, Hold.

practice.prompt: If you tap Shake {n} times in the lab, shakes logged = ?
practice.hint: Each Shake tap in the lab adds one shake to the count.
Get your body low before you cover and hold on.
practice.explain: Drop, then Cover, then Hold until shaking stops.

pool.hint: A sudden shake points to a quake, not ash or wind.
pool.explain: Sudden shake is a quake clue; ash points to a volcano.

pool.hint: Get your body low first — do not run toward glass.
pool.explain: Drop low, then Cover and Hold — avoid glass and shelves.

pool.prompt: In a real quake the ground…

pool.hint: Cartoons exaggerate cracks; real quakes mainly shake.
pool.explain: Shaking is real; forever cartoon canyons are not typical.

pool.hint: Think of Earth's outer shell cracked into big pieces.
pool.explain: Plates are pieces of Earth's outer crust.

pool.prompt: Safety steps in Drop-Cover-Hold (still 3 after {n} drills) = ?
pool.hint: Drop, Cover, and Hold remain three named moves every time.
pool.explain: After {n} drills the plan still has 3 steps.

pool.hint: Stay protected under sturdy cover until shaking stops.

pool.hint: Name the shell plates, then motion, then the shake.
pool.explain: Plates move; that motion can shake the ground — an earthquake.
